statements.t: "We executed well in a dynamic environment, delivering third quarter adjusted EBITDA and margins above the midpoint of our guidance, notwithstanding lower book-and-ship volume," said Brian Deck, Chief Executive Officer.
The commitment to our margin improvement program will continue to drive results even amid inflationary and tariff pressures."

“We are revising our full-year 2026 revenue outlook to reflect lower, near-term CPG-related volume expectations, and at the same time, are increasing the midpoint of our margin guidance as we continue to drive operational efficiencies and disciplined cost management," added Deck.
The Company expects any share repurchases to be balanced to maintain a leverage ratio within the desired long-term range of 2.0 - 2.5x.
At the same time, JBT Marel increased the midpoint of its margin guidance, reflecting strong operational execution and cost management.
The Company also increased the midpoint of its EPS guidance to reflect lower interest expense, taxes, and share count.

We aim to create better outcomes for our diverse customers by optimizing food yield and efficiency, improving food safety and quality, and enhancing uptime and proactive maintenance, all while reducing waste and resource use across the global food supply chain.
Broadening and deepening our product leadership through targeted innovation.
For the full year 2026, the Company continues to expect year-over-year growth in revenue, margins and earnings per share, supported by backlog and operational improvement initiatives.

In the first quarter of 2025, the Company implemented the JBT Marel 2025 Integration Restructuring Plan to achieve a portion of its synergy targets as a result of the Marel acquisition to optimize the overall cost structure for the combined Company on a global basis.
The Company recognized cumulativ e restructuring charges of $48 million through September 30, 2026 and expects to recognize the remaining costs by the end of 2026.
Based on our current capital allocation objectives, we anticipate capital expenditures to be between $100 million and $110 million during 2026.
Our level of capital expenditures varies from time to time as a result of actual and anticipated business conditions.

During 2026, we also expect to incur integration, restructuring, and other synergy-related costs in the range of $50 million to $60 million related to the acquisition of Marel in the first quarter of 2025.
We expect to remain in compliance with all covenants.
